transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Could you tell me what's been bringing you here today?

Well, I guess the main thing is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t be forgetting. Like I’ll miss a heart follow-up appointment, or forget to call the clinic back after they’ve left me a message. And it’s not just medical stuff—last week, or maybe it was the week before, I went to help with a repair and showed up without the right tools, which is embarrassing because I used to be pretty good about that kind of thing. It’s just been happening enough that I thought I’d better come in.
Have you noticed any other changes in your thinking or memory, like trouble finding words, getting lost in familiar places, or feeling confused about time or where you are?

Hmm… word finding? I don’t know. I mean, I’ll have the usual “what was that guy’s name” kind of thing, but I figure everybody gets that. I haven’t, uh, noticed getting lost anywhere I know, not like that.

Time… I can lose track of what day it is if I’m not looking at the calendar, but I’ve always kind of been that way. My wife used to keep the appointments straight—well, not all of them, but she had a better system than me. So I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by confused. I don’t feel like I’m waking up not knowing where I am or anything.
Have you had any trouble planning or organizing things, like managing your schedule or handling more complicated tasks at work or home?

Yeah, planning… I mean, I don’t have a job schedule now, so it’s not like before when everything was written on a board or someone would remind me. But I do mess things up. The big ones are appointments—like the heart follow-up, I just flat-out forgot it. And then the clinic calls and I’m supposed to call back, and I’ll think, “I’ll do it after lunch,” and then, you know, three other things happen and it’s gone.

And with tasks, it’s silly stuff but it matters—like I went to help with a repair and got there without the right tools. I used to be better about that. I had a whole way of setting things out, but lately I’ll get going and assume I have what I need, and then I’m standing there feeling like an idiot.
Have you noticed any problems with your thinking or memory that are affecting your ability to handle everyday tasks, like managing finances, following recipes, or keeping track of your medications?

Yeah, it’s more that I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t. Like the heart follow-up appointment—that one bothered me because it’s important. And the clinic left a message and I meant to call back, but then I got busy with something else and it just disappeared from my head.

I don’t know about recipes or that sort of thing, but everyday stuff, yes. Even helping with a repair—I got all the way there and didn’t have the right tools. Which is ridiculous, because I used to be the guy who had everything laid out. My old toolbox had a place for every little thing… anyway, yeah, those kinds of forgetful things are what brought me in.
Have you been having trouble starting tasks, making decisions, or staying motivated to finish things you start?

Hmm… starting things? I’m not sure. I mean, I can start plenty of things if it pops into my head, sometimes too many things, honestly—like I’ll go out to the garage for one reason and then notice something else and, well, that’s a whole afternoon gone.

Decisions… I don’t know if I’d call it trouble making decisions. My wife used to say I’d decide too fast, actually. Like buying a grill we didn’t need because it was “a good deal,” and then where do you put the thing? But finishing things, yeah, I guess some things don’t get finished right away. Though some of that is just normal, isn’t it? You start cleaning out a drawer and then you find old photos, and next thing you know you’re sitting there remembering people from 40 years ago.

So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big motivation problem, exactly. It’s more I get pulled off course, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or not getting pleasure out of activities you normally like?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m down, exactly. I still like the things I like. I mean, some days are slower, sure, but that’s been true forever, especially when the weather’s bad or there’s nothing much going on.

Pleasure… yeah, I still get a kick out of things. Like if I’m puttering around or talking to somebody, I’m fine. Although sometimes I’ll start one thing and end up somewhere else completely—like I’ll go outside just to check something and then I’m messing with a hose or looking at an old box in the garage—but mood-wise, no, I haven’t really noticed a big change.
Have you ever found yourself confused about where you are, or been unsure of the date, month, or year?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I might walk into a room and think, “Now why did I come in here?” but I know where I am. As far as the date… I don’t always keep track of the exact day unless I’ve got something on the calendar, but I know the month and the year. I haven’t been, you know, lost or thinking I’m somewhere else.
Have you been having trouble keeping track of multiple steps in a task, like following instructions or juggling different parts of a project?

Yeah… I think that happens some. Like if I’m at the bridge table, or one of those Fix-It Friends planning meetings, I sit down meaning to really pay attention, you know, follow along with what everybody’s saying.

But after a bit my mind just kind of… slides off somewhere else. Somebody will be talking about who’s bringing tools or what order we’re doing things in, and then I’ll notice a squeaky chair or start thinking about a hand I played last week, and suddenly I realize I missed half of what was said.

So it’s not that I can’t understand the steps, exactly. It’s more keeping my attention on all of it long enough.
Have you ever felt drowsy, unusually confused, or had trouble staying alert during the day?

Drowsy… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I’ll have a slow patch now and then, especially if I’m sitting too long, like in one of those meetings where someone is going over the same thing three different ways. Then my eyes might get heavy, but I wouldn’t call it unusual.

Confused, no… not like I don’t know what’s going on. I might miss something if I’ve drifted off thinking about something else, but staying alert in the daytime… I don’t think that’s been a big problem.
Have you been finding it harder to stay focused during conversations or meetings, like your mind wanders or you get distracted easily?

Yes, that’s pretty much what happens. I’ll sit down at the bridge table, or at one of those Fix-It Friends planning meetings, and I really do mean to pay attention. I’m not trying to be rude or anything.

But after a little while my mind just kind of… wanders off. Someone’s talking, and then I realize I’ve been thinking about something else entirely, and I’ve missed half of what was said. Then I’m trying to catch up without making it obvious.
Has anyone close to you, like family or friends, mentioned that they’ve noticed changes in your memory or thinking lately?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, nobody’s sat me down and said, “Hey, your memory’s getting worse,” or anything like that.

My wife might say I wasn’t listening, but she’s said that for years, you know? Like if she tells me something while I’m halfway looking for my keys or watching the ball game, then later I’ll ask again and she’ll give me that look. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean by memory or thinking changing.

Friends haven’t really brought it up, no. At bridge they’ll tease anybody who forgets what was played, but that’s just bridge. So… no, I don’t think anyone close to me has mentioned a real change.
Can you think of a time recently when you realized you had forgotten something important shortly after it happened, and how did you handle it?

Yeah… actually, that’s kind of the reason I’m here. I’ll forget things that feel like I really shouldn’t be forgetting.

Like, I had a heart follow-up appointment I was supposed to go to, and then afterward I realized I just… didn’t go. It wasn’t like I decided not to. It was just gone out of my head until it was too late. Then I had to call and explain, which is embarrassing.

And there was another time the clinic called, or I was supposed to call them back—I can’t remember exactly which way it went—but I put it off for a minute because I was doing something else, and then the whole day went by. My wife says I should write everything down, and she’s probably right, but then I have little notes all over and I forget which one matters.

Same with repair jobs. I help out with little fix-it things, and I’ll show up without the right tool, even though I knew what I needed when I left the house. Then I’m standing there like, “Well, that was the whole point of coming prepared.” I usually just go back for it or try to borrow one, but it makes me feel pretty foolish.
Have you noticed any problems with things like managing your medications, keeping track of your bills, or handling money lately?

Well… with bills and money, I don’t know that I’ve had a big problem there lately. My wife keeps a pretty good eye on that sort of thing anyway.

The thing that’s been bothering me more is forgetting things I really shouldn’t. Like I said, I missed that heart follow-up appointment, and then I felt awful having to call and explain. Or I’m supposed to call the clinic back, and I think, “I’ll do it in a minute,” and then somehow it’s later and I never did it.

And with repair jobs, I’ll head out thinking I’m all set, then get there without the tool I needed. That drives me crazy because I knew it before I left. It’s not money exactly, but it’s that same keeping-track-of-things problem.
Have you had trouble starting a task you know you need to do, making decisions about how to proceed with something, or organizing your thoughts when trying to plan something out?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, starting things… sometimes I putter around before I get going, but I’ve always kind of been like that.

Planning something out, it depends what it is. If it’s something simple around the house, I usually just start and figure it out as I go. My wife says that’s not always the best system, but, well, I’ve gotten by. Like with fixing something, half the time you don’t know what you’re dealing with until you’re down there looking at it anyway.

Decisions… I don’t think I’m sitting there unable to decide, no. At least not that I’ve really noticed. I might get sidetracked or start doing one thing and then another, but organizing my thoughts in some big unusual way… I don’t know. Maybe you’d have to ask my wife if it looks different from the outside.
Has anyone who knows you well, like a family member or close friend, ever expressed concern about your memory or thinking abilities?

Yeah, my wife mostly. She’ll say, “You need to keep better track of these things,” and she’s not wrong.

What brings me in is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t—like that heart follow-up appointment, or meaning to call the clinic back and then it’s just gone. And with repair jobs, I’ll get all the way there and realize I didn’t bring the right tool, even though I knew I needed it.

My wife notices that stuff because she’s the one who hears me coming home irritated or sees me scrambling afterward. I don’t know if she’d say “thinking abilities” exactly, but she’s definitely concerned about the forgetting.
Can you recall a time recently when you tried to organize your day or plan out a task step-by-step, and if so, did you find it harder than before to keep track of the steps or stay on track?

Yeah… I mean, step-by-step planning, I’m not sure. But I do notice it when I’m supposed to be paying attention to something.

Like at the bridge table, I sit down meaning to follow everything, and then after a bit my mind just kind of… wanders off. Next thing I know, I’ve missed what somebody played or what they said. Same thing at those Fix-It Friends planning meetings — I go in trying to listen, and then halfway through I realize I don’t know what we just decided.

It’s frustrating, because I’m not trying to ignore anybody. I just lose the thread.
Have you noticed that when you try to organize your day or plan something out, you have trouble keeping all the steps in order or lose track of what comes next?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed it that clearly, like “step one, step two, step three” getting mixed up. I’m not usually making a big list like that.

I tend to just start in on the day and then see what needs doing. My wife’s more the planner—she’ll have things written down on the calendar and little notes. I’ll look at them, and then sometimes I’ll get doing something else around the garage or I’ll stop to move something, and then, well, the day sort of goes a different direction.

But keeping steps in order… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I sit there and can’t figure out what comes next. It’s more that I don’t always stay with the plan, if that makes sense.
Have you found it harder lately to organize or complete tasks that involve multiple steps, like planning a trip, preparing a meal with several parts, or managing a project at home?

I’m not sure I’d say harder lately, exactly. I mean, trips—we don’t really do much of that kind of planning now. Meals, my wife mostly handles, unless I’m just making something simple.

Projects at home… I’ve always kind of done them my own way. I’ll start with one thing, then notice something else that needs fixing, and before you know it I’ve got half the garage pulled apart. But that’s sort of how I’ve always been, you know? My wife says I make more work for myself. She’s probably right.

So… I don’t know if it’s a new problem with multiple steps. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Have you had any trouble lately with things like judging distances, knowing where objects are in relation to each other, or finding your way around places you know well?

Hmm… judging distances? I don’t think so. I mean, I still drive the same roads, park the car—well, I’ve never been great at parking in tight spots, but that’s not new.

Finding my way around places I know… no, I don’t think I’ve gotten lost or anything like that. I go to the same store, same club, same places. Sometimes they move things around in the grocery store and that drives me nuts, but that’s everybody, right?

So… no, I haven’t really noticed trouble like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has difficulty with executive functioning beyond memory issues, such as initiating tasks, decision-making, or organizing complex plans, which could indicate mild neurocognitive disorder or another condition.
doctor.question: Have you had trouble starting a task you know you need to do, making decisions about how to proceed with something, or organizing your thoughts when trying to plan something out?

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, starting things… sometimes I putter around before I get going, but I’ve always kind of been like that.

Planning something out, it depends what it is. If it’s something simple around the house, I usually just start and figure it out as I go. My wife says that’s not always the best system, but, well, I’ve gotten by. Like with fixing something, half the time you don’t know what you’re dealing with until you’re down there looking at it anyway.

Decisions… I don’t think I’m sitting there unable to decide, no. At least not that I’ve really noticed. I might get sidetracked or start doing one thing and then another, but organizing my thoughts in some big unusual way… I don’t know. Maybe you’d have to ask my wife if it looks different from the outside.

doctor.question: Has anyone who knows you well, like a family member or close friend, ever expressed concern about your memory or thinking abilities?

patient.answer:
Yeah, my wife mostly. She’ll say, “You need to keep better track of these things,” and she’s not wrong.

What brings me in is I keep forgetting things I really shouldn’t—like that heart follow-up appointment, or meaning to call the clinic back and then it’s just gone. And with repair jobs, I’ll get all the way there and realize I didn’t bring the right tool, even though I knew I needed it.

My wife notices that stuff because she’s the one who hears me coming home irritated or sees me scrambling afterward. I don’t know if she’d say “thinking abilities” exactly, but she’s definitely concerned about the forgetting.

doctor.question: Can you recall a time recently when you tried to organize your day or plan out a task step-by-step, and if so, did you find it harder than before to keep track of the steps or stay on track?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, step-by-step planning, I’m not sure. But I do notice it when I’m supposed to be paying attention to something.

Like at the bridge table, I sit down meaning to follow everything, and then after a bit my mind just kind of… wanders off. Next thing I know, I’ve missed what somebody played or what they said. Same thing at those Fix-It Friends planning meetings — I go in trying to listen, and then halfway through I realize I don’t know what we just decided.

It’s frustrating, because I’m not trying to ignore anybody. I just lose the thread.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that I’ve noticed it that clearly, like “step one, step two, step three” getting mixed up. I’m not usually making a big list like that.

I tend to just start in on the day and then see what needs doing. My wife’s more the planner—she’ll have things written down on the calendar and little notes. I’ll look at them, and then sometimes I’ll get doing something else around the garage or I’ll stop to move something, and then, well, the day sort of goes a different direction.

But keeping steps in order… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I sit there and can’t figure out what comes next. It’s more that I don’t always stay with the plan, if that makes sense.

Projects at home… I’ve always kind of done them my own way. I’ll start with one thing, then notice something else that needs fixing, and before you know it I’ve got half the garage pulled apart. Hmm… judging distances? I don’t think so. I mean, I still drive the same roads, park the car—well, I’ve never been great at parking in tight spots, but that’s not new.

Finding my way around places I know… no, I don’t think I’ve gotten lost or anything like that. I go to the same store, same club, same places. Sometimes they move things around in the grocery store and that drives me nuts, but that’s everybody, right?

These deficits are not better explained by delirium, neurocognitive disorder due to another medical condition, or substance use. The cognitive deficits appear acquired and represent a decline from previous levels of functioning, consistent with major neurocognitive disorder due to Alzheimer's disease or similar pathology. The absence of prominent mood symptoms rules out F07.81 (personality change), and the lack of clear organic cause or substance use makes F06.7 (mild neurocognitive disorder due to physiological condition) less likely.
